fair_value.method: Blend of three sum-of-the-parts views on a pro forma post-VAC basis (~326M shares = 249.9M at 6/30/26 + ~9.6M ASM + 65.85M VAC; pro forma net debt incl. $700M 0.75% converts, $135M VAC preferred and VAC debt of roughly $0.8B): conservative cash-flow SOTP $7.1 (40%), peer-multiple SOTP $9.8 (35%), risked-NAV SOTP using company project NPVs $12.0 (25%), which gives about $9.3.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Conservative cash-flow SOTP. Uranium: ~1.75M lb/yr sold at ~$85 realized, ~$40/lb all-in cost, so ~$80M EBITDA x 11x = $0.9B, plus US development assets (Roca Honda, Bullfrog, Nichols Ranch, Alta Mesa) $0.3B, total $1.2B. VAC: FY25 adj. EBITDA $29M ramping to ~$80M in 2027 (Sumter 2,000 tpa at $65-75M run-rate) x ~15x (credit for growth), about $1.2B EV. Rare earths: White Mesa REE + heavy-REE circuits $0.3B; ASM (Korean Metals Plant + Dubbo) $0.15B; Donald 49% option, risked, $0.15B; Vara Mada at 20% of $1.8B NPV = $0.36B; Bahia $0.05B; total ~$1.0B. Corporate overhead -$40M/yr x 8 = -$0.3B. EV $3.1B minus net debt ~$0.8B = $2.3B / 326M sh.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Peer-multiple SOTP (valued like the market prices US uranium/Western REE names). Uranium platform $1.8B (~20x 2027 EBITDA, in line with US producer peers that trade on in-ground lbs); REE/magnet platform $2.5B (VAC $1.4B + upstream REE/ASM/Donald/Vara Mada $1.1B, a strategic-supply premium similar to MP-type multiples); overhead -$0.3B. EV $4.0B minus net debt $0.8B = $3.2B / 326M sh.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Risked NAV using company project economics: Vara Mada $1.8B NPV x 35%; Donald 49% x A$2.3B pre-tax NPV8 x ~0.7 after tax x 40% risk less funding; uranium NAV $1.5B; VAC at deal cost ~$1.6B (cash $718M + 65.85M sh at ~$11.35 + $135M pref); White Mesa REE/ASM $0.5B; overhead -$0.3B. EV ~$5.0B minus net debt $0.8B, then minus ~$0.2B dilution for near-term ATM/capex = ~$3.9B / 326M sh.

bear.story: Uranium eases toward $70s and White Mesa runs stay lumpy. VAC closes with the $135M preferred kicker and ~66M new shares, and integration costs plus Sumter ramp delays keep consolidated EBITDA negative. Donald FID slips again and the Madagascar agreement stalls. NdPr stays below $100/kg and further ATM issuance is needed, so the market values UUUU as uranium plus cash plus a leveraged, loss-making magnet business.

base.story: Uranium holds $85-95 (LT price at a record ~$96.50), 2027 sales of ~1.5-2M lb at ~57% gross margin. VAC closes in early 2027 and 2027 EBITDA of ~$60-80M is roughly break-even for the group after overhead. Heavy-REE circuit construction stays on track for late 2027. The strategic premium persists but does not expand, and the stock trades around a blended SOTP of $9-12.

bull.story: A US/allied policy shock (Chinese export controls, DoD price floors, Section 232 action) re-rates Western mine-to-magnet platforms. Donald reaches FID and the Vara Mada investment agreement is signed. Terbium/dysprosium qualification with Japanese magnet makers turns into contracts, uranium runs above $100, and the stock revisits the prior 52-week high region ($20-28), which is near analyst targets ($16-33).

thesis_break_reason: At ~$6 the pre-VAC equity (~260M sh, ~$1.56B) would be worth only about net cash plus the uranium business. The market would then be assigning zero or negative value to the rare-earth/magnet platform, which would most likely mean something fundamental broke: the VAC deal or financing failed, a large discounted equity raise, a collapse in the uranium price or White Mesa operating problems. Ordinary volatility at 70-90% could still reach it, but it would mark the end of the integrated-platform thesis.

catalysts.event: Donald Project (Astron JV) final investment decision, already delayed from Q2/Q3 2026, plus A$220M EFA debt package
Q3-2026 results (uranium sales volumes/realized price, ASM consolidation, integration costs)
White Mesa Mill uranium processing campaign resumes after maintenance
VAC acquisition closing (regulatory approvals); issuance of 65.85M shares + up to $135M preferred since price < $20.93; Goldman $250M term loan
FY2026 results and 2027 uranium/REE guidance, first consolidated magnet guidance
Madagascar government investment agreement for Vara Mada (parliament/High Court approval)
US critical-minerals policy: DoD NdPr price floor, Section 232 on magnets, China export-control changes; Office of Strategic Capital $725M loan finalization
Q2-2027 results; status of Tb/Dy circuit (target end-2027)

key_uncertainties: VAC economics and integration: paying ~$1.6-1.9B for a business with $29M FY25 adjusted EBITDA relies on the Sumter ramp to $65-75M and then $130-140M
Dilution: ~26% more shares from VAC, the preferred kicker below $20.93, ATM usage (8.4M shares in H1-26), and $700M converts at $20.34
Uranium price path and lumpy mill campaigns / sales timing
Execution and jurisdiction risk on Donald (FID still pending), Vara Mada (post-coup Madagascar) and Bahia
Sentiment/policy-driven rare-earth premium, which can swing the stock ±50% independent of fundamentals
NdPr pricing (~$96/kg, below the $110/kg DoD floor) and heavy-REE market access vs Chinese supply
reasoning: UUUU (Energy Fuels) is a low-cost US uranium producer (~$23/lb production cost in Q2-26, 57% gross margin, H1-26 output 1.7M lb, inventory ~2.27M lb) that is turning itself into a mine-to-magnet rare-earth platform through the ASM acquisition (closed Aug 28, 2026) and the $1.9B VAC acquisition (signed Jun 23, 2026, closing early 2027: $718M cash + 65.85M shares + up to $135M preferred). The stock fell from ~$16 at the VAC announcement to $11.35 on dilution/valuation worries, a Q2 miss (EPS -$0.13 vs -$0.03, with $10.7M deal costs) and a sector pullback, even though spot uranium is strong (~$90/lb, LT ~$96.50). My valuation is on a pro forma basis: about $960M of cash/securities mostly goes to VAC cash consideration and capex, which leaves roughly $0.8B pro forma net debt (converts + preferred + VAC debt) and ~326M shares. The three SOTP views range from $7.1 (cash-flow multiples) to $12.0 (risked company NPVs), blended to ~$9.3, which is below the current price. The market (and sell-side, avg target ~$24 but low $16) is paying a strategic premium for Western rare-earth optionality that I only partly credit. Against that, uranium fundamentals are solid, the insider (CEO) bought ~$1M at ~$15-16, and policy shocks can re-rate the group quickly, as the $27.90 high shows. For the distribution I used a lognormal with median ~$10.2 (slightly below spot, reflecting a fair value under the price, VAC-close dilution and dilution/financing overhang, partly offset by uranium strength) and sigma ~0.68. That sigma is below the 89% realized vol because some of the past year's vol came from one-off policy spikes, but it is well above the large-cap 25-35% base rate. I trimmed the extreme left tail slightly to allow for financing-crash risk. Scenario mean (~$11.9) is close to spot, consistent with a roughly fair-to-slightly-rich stock with a fat right tail. Research was via web search/fetch only; no option data was used.
